title: NOSE LANDING GEAR SHOCK STRUT - SERVICING
question: What are the detailed steps for inspecting and adjusting the hydraulic fluid level and inflation pressure of the nose gear shock strut during maintenance?
answer: Service the nose gear shock strut as follows: (1) Remove the air valve cap and release all air. Remove the air valve housing assembly. (3) Compress the strut fully until the strut's bottom fork touches the top barrel housing. Examine the hydraulic fluid level and add fluid as necessary. Fluid used must agree with specification MIL-PRF-5606. Make sure the hydraulic fluid level is at the bottom of the air valve installation hole. Install the air valve housing assembly. With strut fully extended and the nose wheel off of the ground, inflate the strut to 55 to 60 PSI. The nose landing gear shock strut will use only minimum service. Strut extension pressure must be kept at 55 to 60 PSI. Use a clean, lint-free cloth soaked with MIL- PRF-5606 or kerosene to clean the machined surfaces of dirt and dust.
